title: Profile React render cycles via performance trace
description: Use chrome-devtools MCP to capture a performance trace while interacting with the app. Identify components with excessive re-renders, particularly Sidebar (known over-subscription), and quantify render frequency.
action: Start performance trace via chrome-devtools MCP, trigger common interactions (open conversation, switch tabs, type in editor), stop trace, analyze results to identify re-render hotspots. Write findings to render-profile.json.

criteria: render-profile.json contains at least 3 components with render frequency data
Sidebar.tsx is listed in render hotspots if render count > 10 during trace
convergence.verification: Read render-profile.json and verify it contains component render data
convergence.definition_of_done: React render cycle profile captured with re-render hotspots identified

files.change: Create JSON file with component render counts and hotspot analysis

implementation: Ensure dev server is running (shared with TASK-001)
Use chrome-devtools MCP: performance_start_trace to begin profiling
Use chrome-devtools MCP: navigate/interact to trigger common user flows
Use chrome-devtools MCP: performance_stop_trace to capture trace
Use chrome-devtools MCP: performance_analyze_insight to extract render data
Parse trace data for React component render counts

success_metrics: Render profile contains data for >= 3 components

reference.pattern: Chrome DevTools Performance API via MCP

rationale.chosen_approach: chrome-devtools performance trace provides actual render timing without needing React DevTools extension
rationale.tradeoffs: Less detailed than React DevTools Profiler (no component-level render causes)

risks: Performance trace may not capture React-specific render data

affected_requirements: SC-6: Priority optimization list with impact estimates
